name: India
notice: Starter index of well-known Indian provisions and landmark Supreme Court decisions. Summaries are paraphrased for retrieval and are NOT the statutory text. Always verify against the official bare act (indiacode.nic.in) and a law report before relying on any provision or precedent. Add fuller packs under LEGAL_PACKS_DIR.
prompt_notes: Offences committed on or after 1 July 2024 are governed by the BNS, BNSS and BSA; earlier conduct is governed by the IPC, CrPC and Indian Evidence Act.
Do not invent section numbers or case names. If you are unsure of a citation, argue from the evidence and say that the authority should be checked.

procedure_notes.charge: The court frames the charge and the accused is asked to plead (Chapter on trial before a Court of Session, BNSS).
procedure_notes.accused_statement: The court examines the accused on the incriminating circumstances in the evidence (BNSS s.351, formerly CrPC s.313).
procedure_notes.judgment: The judgment states the points for determination, the decision on each and the reasons.

provisions.title: Equality before law
provisions.summary: The State shall not deny any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within India.

provisions.title: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
provisions.summary: Guarantees citizens the freedoms of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence and profession, subject to reasonable restrictions.

provisions.title: Protection in respect of conviction for offences
provisions.summary: No ex post facto criminal law (20(1)), no double jeopardy (20(2)) and no compulsion to be a witness against oneself (20(3)).

provisions.title: Protection of life and personal liberty
provisions.summary: No person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law; read with Maneka Gandhi, that procedure must be fair, just and reasonable.

provisions.title: Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases
provisions.summary: A person arrested must be told the grounds, may consult and be defended by a lawyer of choice and must be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours; preventive detention is separately regulated.

provisions.title: Remedies for enforcement of fundamental rights
provisions.summary: The right to move the Supreme Court directly for enforcement of fundamental rights, including by writs.

provisions.title: Equal justice and free legal aid
provisions.summary: Directive principle that the State secure equal justice and provide free legal aid so that opportunities are not denied by economic or other disabilities.

provisions.title: Special leave to appeal by the Supreme Court
provisions.summary: The Supreme Court may grant special leave to appeal from any judgment, decree or order of any court or tribunal in India.

provisions.title: Law declared by Supreme Court to be binding on all courts
provisions.summary: The law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts within the territory of India.

provisions.title: Enforcement of decrees and orders of the Supreme Court
provisions.summary: The Supreme Court may pass such decree or order as is necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter before it.

provisions.title: Power of High Courts to issue certain writs
provisions.summary: High Courts may issue writs for enforcement of fundamental rights and for any other purpose.

provisions.title: General explanations
provisions.summary: Contains general explanatory provisions, including sub-section (5): when a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of the common intention of all, each is liable as if done by him alone.

provisions.title: Act of a child under seven years of age
provisions.summary: Nothing is an offence which is done by a child under seven years of age.

provisions.title: Act of a person of unsound mind
provisions.summary: Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, by reason of unsoundness of mind, is incapable of knowing the nature of the act or that it is wrong or contrary to law.

provisions.title: Things done in private defence
provisions.summary: Nothing is an offence which is done in the exercise of the right of private defence.

provisions.title: Right of private defence of the body and of property
provisions.summary: Every person has a right, subject to restrictions, to defend his own body and that of another, and property, against specified offences.

provisions.title: Criminal conspiracy
provisions.summary: Defines criminal conspiracy as an agreement to do or cause to be done an illegal act, or a legal act by illegal means, and prescribes its punishment.

provisions.title: Rape
provisions.summary: Defines the offence of rape and the circumstances in which sexual intercourse is rape, including the position on consent.

provisions.title: Punishment for rape
provisions.summary: Prescribes rigorous imprisonment and fine for rape, with enhanced punishment in aggravated circumstances.

provisions.title: Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
provisions.summary: Punishes assault or use of criminal force on a woman intending to outrage, or knowing it likely to outrage, her modesty.

provisions.title: Sexual harassment
provisions.summary: Punishes unwelcome physical contact and advances, demands for sexual favours, showing pornography against will and sexually coloured remarks.

provisions.title: Dowry death
provisions.summary: Where a woman's death is caused by burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than in normal circumstances within seven years of marriage, and she was subjected to cruelty or harassment for dowry soon before death, the husband or relative is deemed to have caused the death.

provisions.title: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty
provisions.summary: Punishes cruelty by a husband or his relative towards a woman, including conduct driving her to suicide and harassment to coerce unlawful demands.

provisions.title: Culpable homicide
provisions.summary: Defines culpable homicide: causing death by an act done with the intention of causing death or such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with knowledge that it is likely to cause death.

provisions.title: Murder
provisions.summary: Defines murder as culpable homicide that meets specified conditions (such as intention to cause death or bodily injury sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death), subject to the listed exceptions.

provisions.title: Punishment for murder
provisions.summary: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and fine.

provisions.title: Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder
provisions.summary: Prescribes imprisonment for life or for a term of not less than five years, and fine, depending on the limb of the definition satisfied.

provisions.title: Causing death by negligence
provisions.summary: Punishes causing death by a rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, with an enhanced penalty for rash and negligent driving followed by escape.

provisions.title: Abetment of suicide
provisions.summary: Punishes a person who abets the commission of suicide.

provisions.title: Attempt to murder
provisions.summary: Punishes an act done with the intention or knowledge, and in circumstances, that would make the actor guilty of murder had death been caused.

provisions.title: Voluntarily causing hurt
provisions.summary: Defines and punishes voluntarily causing hurt, with a higher penalty for grievous hurt under the later provisions.

provisions.title: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt
provisions.summary: Punishes voluntarily causing grievous hurt, with enhanced punishment where it results in permanent disability or a persistent vegetative state.

provisions.title: Kidnapping
provisions.summary: Defines kidnapping from India and kidnapping from lawful guardianship and provides for punishment.

provisions.title: Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
provisions.summary: Punishes acts, by words, signs or otherwise, that excite secession, armed rebellion or subversive activities or endanger the sovereignty or unity of India; it takes the place of the former sedition offence.

provisions.title: Unlawful assembly
provisions.summary: Defines an assembly of five or more persons with a common unlawful object and punishes membership.

provisions.title: Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object
provisions.summary: If an offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly in prosecution of the common object, every member who was then a member is guilty of that offence.

provisions.title: Rioting
provisions.summary: Defines and punishes rioting, being the use of force or violence by an unlawful assembly or any member of it in prosecution of the common object.

provisions.title: Theft
provisions.summary: Defines theft as dishonestly taking movable property out of the possession of any person without consent, and prescribes its punishment.

provisions.title: Robbery
provisions.summary: Defines robbery as theft or extortion accompanied by, or attended with, instant hurt, wrongful restraint or fear of instant death, hurt or restraint, and punishes it.

provisions.title: Dacoity
provisions.summary: Defines dacoity as robbery committed or attempted by five or more persons jointly, and punishes it.

provisions.title: Criminal breach of trust
provisions.summary: Defines criminal breach of trust, involving dishonest misappropriation of property entrusted to a person, and prescribes punishment, with aggravated forms.

provisions.title: Cheating
provisions.summary: Defines cheating as deceiving a person and fraudulently or dishonestly inducing delivery of property or an act or omission, with enhanced punishment for cheating that induces delivery of property.

provisions.title: Cheating by personation
provisions.summary: Defines and punishes cheating by pretending to be another person or knowingly substituting one person for another.

provisions.title: Criminal intimidation
provisions.summary: Defines criminal intimidation as threatening a person with injury to person, reputation or property with intent to cause alarm, and punishes it, with aggravated forms.

provisions.title: Defamation
provisions.summary: Defines defamation by words, signs or visible representation harming reputation, lists exceptions and prescribes punishment.

provisions.title: When police may arrest without warrant
provisions.summary: Sets out the cases in which a police officer may arrest without an order from a Magistrate and without a warrant, including the notice-of-appearance route for offences punishable up to seven years.

provisions.title: Audio-video recording of search and seizure
provisions.summary: Requires the process of search and seizure to be recorded through audio-video electronic means, with the recording forwarded promptly to the Magistrate.

provisions.title: Information in cognizable cases (FIR)
provisions.summary: Governs registration of information relating to a cognizable offence (FIR), including electronic information and a preliminary enquiry in certain cases.

provisions.title: Examination of witnesses by police
provisions.summary: Allows a police officer investigating an offence to examine orally any person acquainted with the facts and circumstances of the case.

provisions.title: Recording of confessions and statements
provisions.summary: Provides for recording of confessions and statements by a Magistrate during investigation, with safeguards to ensure they are voluntary.

provisions.title: Procedure when investigation cannot be completed in twenty-four hours
provisions.summary: Governs production of an arrested person before a Magistrate and remand/detention while investigation continues, with outer limits on custody.

provisions.title: Report of police officer on completion of investigation
provisions.summary: Requires the police officer, on completion of investigation, to forward a report (the charge-sheet or final report) to the Magistrate.

provisions.title: Power to examine the accused
provisions.summary: Empowers the court to question the accused on the circumstances appearing in the evidence against him so that he may explain them; the accused is not sworn and cannot be penalised for refusing to answer.

provisions.title: Maximum period for which an undertrial prisoner can be detained
provisions.summary: Limits detention of undertrial prisoners, who become entitled to bail after serving a stated fraction of the maximum sentence, subject to conditions.

provisions.title: When bail may be taken in case of non-bailable offence
provisions.summary: Sets out when and on what conditions a person accused of a non-bailable offence may be released on bail.

provisions.title: Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest
provisions.summary: Allows the High Court or Court of Session to direct that a person apprehending arrest for a non-bailable offence be released on bail if arrested (anticipatory bail).

provisions.title: Special powers of High Court or Court of Session regarding bail
provisions.summary: Gives the High Court and Court of Session special powers to grant bail and to set conditions or modify bail orders.

provisions.title: Confession caused by inducement, threat or promise
provisions.summary: A confession made by an accused is irrelevant in a criminal proceeding if it appears to the court to have been caused by inducement, threat, coercion or promise from a person in authority.

provisions.title: Confession to police officer and confession in custody
provisions.summary: A confession to a police officer cannot be proved against the accused, and a confession by a person in police custody is inadmissible unless made in the immediate presence of a Magistrate, subject to the proviso that information leading to discovery of a fact may be proved to the extent it relates distinctly to that fact.

provisions.title: Admissibility of electronic or digital record
provisions.summary: An electronic or digital record is not to be denied admissibility merely because it is such a record; it has the same legal effect, validity and enforceability as other documents.

provisions.title: Admissibility of electronic records
provisions.summary: Provides the conditions and the certificate requirement under which the contents of an electronic record are admissible as documentary evidence.

provisions.title: Burden of proof
provisions.summary: Whoever desires any court to give judgment as to a legal right or liability dependent on the existence of facts he asserts must prove that those facts exist.

provisions.title: Burden of proving a fact especially within the knowledge of a person
provisions.summary: When a fact is especially within the knowledge of any person, the burden of proving that fact is upon him.

cases.name: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
cases.holding: Parliament may amend the Constitution but cannot alter its basic structure.

cases.name: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
cases.holding: Procedure depriving a person of liberty under Article 21 must be fair, just and reasonable; Articles 14, 19 and 21 are interrelated.

cases.name: Hussainara Khatoon v. Home Secretary, State of Bihar
cases.holding: Speedy trial is part of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21; prolonged undertrial detention is unjust.

cases.name: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab
cases.holding: The death penalty is constitutionally valid but to be imposed only in the rarest of rare cases, weighing aggravating and mitigating circumstances.

cases.name: Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra
cases.holding: Sets out the conditions for a conviction resting on circumstantial evidence: circumstances must be fully established, consistent only with guilt and form a complete chain.

cases.name: Joginder Kumar v. State of U.P.
cases.holding: The power to arrest is distinct from its justification; arrest should not be routine and requires reasonable satisfaction.

cases.name: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal
cases.holding: Lays down binding guidelines to be followed on arrest and detention to prevent custodial torture and deaths.

cases.name: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan
cases.holding: Issued guidelines against sexual harassment at the workplace, grounded in Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21.

cases.name: State of Maharashtra v. Praful B. Desai
cases.holding: Evidence of a witness may be recorded by video conferencing, which satisfies the requirement of presence.

cases.name: Selvi v. State of Karnataka
cases.holding: Involuntary narco-analysis, polygraph and brain-mapping tests violate the right against self-incrimination under Article 20(3) and personal liberty under Article 21.

cases.name: Sanjay Chandra v. CBI
cases.holding: Bail is the rule and jail the exception; pre-trial detention must not be punitive and the gravity of the offence alone does not justify refusing bail.

cases.name: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
cases.holding: Police must not arrest automatically in offences punishable up to seven years; they must apply the statutory checklist and record reasons.

cases.name: Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh
cases.holding: Registration of an FIR is mandatory when information discloses a cognizable offence; a preliminary inquiry is permitted only in limited categories.

cases.name: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
cases.holding: Struck down Section 66A of the Information Technology Act as violating Article 19(1)(a).

cases.name: K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India
cases.holding: The right to privacy is a fundamental right under Articles 14, 19 and 21.

cases.name: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
cases.holding: Section 377 IPC was held unconstitutional insofar as it criminalised consensual same-sex conduct between adults.

cases.name: Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal
cases.holding: A certificate under Section 65B(4) of the Evidence Act is a mandatory condition for admitting secondary electronic evidence, except where the original device is produced.
